text:
Marathon Petroleum's stock jumped 2.3% today, continuing a sharp run-up that has gained nearly 14% over the past two weeks. The move reflects surging diesel prices and tight global diesel supplies—refiners like Marathon profit when the spread between crude oil input costs and refined product selling prices widens, and diesel in particular is commanding premium prices due to Middle East supply disruptions and low U.S. diesel inventory (105 million barrels). Political pressure to ease diesel prices through stockpile releases and export restrictions, combined with tanker shortages driving shipping costs to 10 times historical levels, has tightened margins and boosted refiner valuations.

U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity, near full utilization, which means Marathon and peers are operating profitably but with little room to ramp output further. The global supply crunch—especially the attacks on tankers in the Persian Gulf and the shortage of available shipping—is keeping diesel scarce and expensive relative to crude, a dynamic that favors refiners' bottom lines as long as crude prices don't spike further to offset the product gains.
